transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-02-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Samir Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM); Jordan Lee (Nimbus CTO), Priya Nair (Nimbus ML Eng), Evan Soto (Nimbus Platform), Marta Ruiz (Nimbus Security)

Automatic Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): quick check on onboarding, some access missing, small perf wins with quantized model, still need vpc peering + KMS; next run planned.

[00:00:00] Alex (AE - Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. quick agenda — onboarding status, access confirmations, initial perf notes, then next steps. how's everybody?
[00:00:12] Jordan (CTO - Nimbus): Yep all good, thanks. we have Priya and Evan on to go through the env details. Marta is here for any security questions.
[00:00:20] Priya (ML Eng): hi all. we did the sample inference yesterday, saw some interesting latencies, will share logs after this.
[00:00:28] Samir (SE - Redwood): great, that helps. first question — did you get the service account and the test keys we sent last week? i see partial access in the console but not full cluster creds.
[00:00:40] Evan (Platform): we set up the service account but the kube context wasn't provided yet; we're waiting on the final role binding.
[00:00:48] Alex: ok that's one of the blockers for running full perf. Jordan, any timeline on role binding and VPC peering?
[00:00:56] Jordan: our infra team is tied up but we can prioritize this week; aiming 48 hours.
[00:01:05] Maya (CSM): perfect, that aligns with the pilot window. also reminder — we'll need the audit-log access to validate retention settings.
[00:01:15] Marta (Security): yes, on audit logs — we need to confirm where logs land and encryption at rest details (KMS). is Redwood using customer-managed keys or your default?
[00:01:25] Alex: we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; for Hosted we have envelope encryption, but for Dedicated/Private you can bring keys — we'll send the KMS integration doc.
[00:01:38] Priya: great, please send that. also curious about model variants — we tried the 13B open model and saw some high tail latencies beyond 95th. any recommended tuning?
[00:01:48] Samir: yes, a few quick wins — smaller context window, KV cache warmup, and quantized variant. with our runtime the 8-bit quantized model often reduces tail latency by 20-30% on similar GPUs.
[00:02:01] Priya: when you say KV cache warmup, you mean prefix caching? our requests are fairly short, most are 80-120 tokens.
[00:02:08] Samir: right, prefix/KV caching helps if you have repeated contexts; for short requests batching policy matters more. our suggestions will be in the benchmark template.
[00:02:18] [00:02:18] Jordan: any concerns about quality when moving to a quantized model? we can't degrade user experience.
[00:02:25] Samir: generally quality delta is small for many tasks; we'll run side-by-side evals on your prompt set — Redwood Optimize will flag any regressions against your golden prompts.
[00:02:36] Priya: ok good. we did notice some transcription/label noise in the logs, e.g., 'Redood' in a couple traces — not sure if that was test artifact.
[00:02:45] Alex: heh, yeah transcription can be messy. unrelated but noted.
[00:02:50] [00:02:50] Samir: on environment readiness — i have a checklist: 1) VPC peering complete, 2) service account + kube context, 3) GPU nodes reserved (we recommend 1-2 p4-like nodes for pilot), 4) storage access for model weights, 5) KMS access for customer keys. which of these are done?
[00:03:08] Evan: storage and partial GPU reservation done; VPC peering in progress; KMS still pending legal approval.
[00:03:16] Marta: KMS depends on our security review; we have a quick question — will Redwood's control plane see raw requests in the Private deployment?
[00:03:24] Alex: for Private we can run control plane in customer VPC or on-prem; by default the control plane metadata is visible for operational telemetry but we offer opt-out and can route telemetry into your logging. we'll document that precisely.
[00:03:38] Priya: can you share an example of the telemetry fields? request IDs, latency buckets, token counts?
[00:03:44] Samir: yes — we'll share a sample trace and schema. it includes request id, model version, token counts, per-token latency buckets (est.), and error types.
[00:03:55] [00:03:55] Jordan: sounds good. next up — perf results. Priya, you said you ran 500 sample requests? any numbers?
[00:04:03] Priya: yes, quick run with the default 13B; median latency ~220ms but 95th was ~1.8s — that's the main concern. throughput was low under concurrent load.
[00:04:14] Samir: that matches typical warm-cold behavior. was the KV cache empty on that run?
[00:04:20] Priya: yes it was cold. we didn't maintain a warm instance.
[00:04:23] Samir: ok, so we'll recommend a warmup step and continuous batching during tests. also confirm which GPU type — that affects kernel selection.
[00:04:32] Priya: we're on aT4 equivalent in our lab; not ideal for large models.
[00:04:36] Samir: that explains tail — p4/p5 class GPUs will help. also quantization options will reduce memory and improve perf.
[00:04:43] [00:04:43] Jordan: cost question — can you ballpark cost for running a small pilot with 2 p4 nodes for two weeks?
[00:04:50] Alex: i'll send a pilot pricing estimate; rough ballpark is in the deck but i'll put numbers in the spreadsheet — will include reserved vs burst options.
[00:04:59] Priya: for tuning, can we test both model 13B float and 13B-8bit q?
[00:05:05] Samir: yes, we'll stage runs for both and do A/B on quality metrics. please share your eval prompts (golden set).
[00:05:12] Priya: will send later today.
[00:05:15] [00:05:15] Maya: quick note on timeline — if VPC peering and creds are done by Fri (48hrs), we can schedule the perf run early next week.
[00:05:24] Jordan: that's fine.
[00:05:27] Marta: security quick Q — you mentioned audit logs and retention; what are default retention windows?
[00:05:33] Alex: defaults vary by deployment; Hosted has 30 days by default, Dedicated can be configurable up to 1 year with add-on. we'll send the retention doc and SOC2 artifact link.
[00:05:45] [00:05:45] Priya: also saw a couple of errors in the logs — rate-limited responses flagged as 429 during concurrent bursts — were those client-side or on the runtime?
[00:05:54] Samir: initial hypothesis — our autoscaler hadn't seen the spike because cluster wasn't registered fully; once the control plane sees the metrics it will autoscale. we'll confirm in the next run.
[00:06:05] Evan: noted — we'll watch the autoscaler logs and forward them.
[00:06:09] [00:06:09] Alex: another small thing — prompt formatting. we noticed some requests include long system tokens which are repeated. trimming system tokens can reduce per-request compute.
[00:06:20] Priya: ok we have some legacy wrappers that add context; we'll try to reduce that during testing.
[00:06:26] [00:06:26] Samir: about benchmarks — Samir: sending benchmark template includes target SLOs (p50/p95), concurrency model, and step-by-step to reproduce. also will include a small load generator script.
[00:06:38] Jordan: will the script run from our infra or do you provide hosted harness?
[00:06:43] Samir: you can run locally against your cluster; we also offer a managed runner if you prefer us to kick off the test. for initial tests, local runner is easiest.
[00:06:52] [00:06:52] Priya: any logs schema for error traces? we want to correlate user-facing errors with model responses.
[00:06:58] Samir: yes, we'll provide a mapping; we also add per-token timing which helps find attention spikes.
[00:07:05] [00:07:05] Alex: ok let's talk about compliance docs — Marta, anything specific you need from Redwood to progress KMS approval?
[00:07:12] Marta: sample SOC2 evidence, encryption-at-rest details, and clarification on whether metadata will be retained by Redwood. also contractual language for data residency.
[00:07:23] Alex: we'll attach SOC2 report excerpts and a short doc on metadata handling. legal can provide data residency clauses for Private deployment.
[00:07:31] [00:07:31] Jordan: quick ask — can we try a small test with the dedicated runtime but keep data in our VPC?
[00:07:38] Samir: yes, Dedicated with VPC peering works; if you want full separation we can deploy Private with customer-managed control plane. both options available.
[00:07:47] Priya: for the pilot we'll start with Dedicated + VPC peering.
[00:07:51] [00:07:51] Samir: perfect. i'll note GPU recommendations: for 13B we suggest 1 p4dn per 6-8 concurrent short requests, but exact depends on token distribution.
[00:08:02] Priya: that's helpful.
[00:08:05] [00:08:05] Alex: ok wrapping up — recap and next steps. Alex: we'll share pilot pricing + timeline, Samir will send benchmark template and load script, Jordan/Evan will finish VPC peering and provide creds, Priya will send golden prompts and initial logs, Marta will confirm security checklist items.
[00:08:22] Jordan: sounds good.
[00:08:24] Priya: one more tiny item — do you have an example of RBAC roles for service account?
[00:08:30] Samir: yes we'll include a minimal rolebinding yaml in the benchmark repo.
[00:08:35] [00:08:35] Alex: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email and Slack.

[00:30:00] [note: meeting continued with troubleshooting access gap and a brief demo of monitoring UI]
[00:30:05] Samir: demoing the trace view — this is request id, token timing, kernel choice heuristics. (audio)
[00:30:20] Priya: i'm seeing the trace; the per-token spikes line up with our slower tails.
[00:30:33] Samir: yep that suggests kernel choice on those sequence lengths is suboptimal; we can force a different kernel selection for the test.
[00:30:45] Jordan: great — can you force it for the next run?
[00:30:51] Samir: yes, we'll configure runtime flags for the perf run.
[00:31:05] [00:31:05] Evan: access update — rolebinding created, test service account creds sent to Samir via secure link.
[00:31:15] Samir: got them, thanks. i'll validate and kick off a warmup.
[00:31:22] Priya: will monitor as you run.
[00:31:28] [00:31:28] Maya: just to confirm, next run target is early next week with 10k samples?
[00:31:34] Samir: target is 10k sample run with A/B variants, yes — we'll coordinate exact timing in the calendar.
[00:31:42] Jordan: fine.
[00:31:45] [00:31:45] Alex: any blockers from Redwood side?
[00:31:49] Samir: only validation of the creds; otherwise ready to run.
[00:31:54] Alex: ok if no more questions we'll close. thanks all.

Final recap (auto):
- Blockers: VPC peering (in flight), KMS approval (security), role binding (done during call)
- Next perf run: early next week, goal 10k sample A/B test across float vs quantized 13B
- Deliverables: pricing & pilot plan, benchmark template + load script, SOC2/retention docs
